name: Scituate
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Scituate, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Scituate, MA: Santa's boat arrival at Holidays in the Harbor, a drive-in holiday movie, the Holiday Pops and Lawson Tower bells.
lede: Scituate does Christmas by the water, with Santa arriving by boat in Scituate Harbor and a tree made of lobster buoys, and on First Parish Road, where Christmas music rings out from the bells of Lawson Tower.
celebrates: Scituate's holiday season centers on Scituate Harbor, where the Scituate Harbor Business Association runs Holidays in the Harbor along Front Street and Cole Parkway. The weekend opens with a First Friday evening of music, hayrides, tree lightings and shopping, and on Saturday morning Santa arrives by boat. The Scituate Visitors Center describes carriage rides with Clydesdales, a wreath contest, gingerbread house displays and a Lobster Trap Tree of hand-painted buoys. Away from the water, the Scituate Historical Society plays Christmas music on the Lawson Tower bells, and South Shore Conservatory brings its Holiday Pops to the Scituate Performing Arts Center.
lastyear: In 2025 Holidays in the Harbor fell on the first weekend of December. On Friday, December 5, 2025, the Scituate Harbor Business Association posted its evening lineup, promising horse and carriage rides, kids crafts, live performances, giveaways, cocktails and tree lightings, with the harbor buzzing all evening, and said the Saturday events would follow in a separate post. The 2026 weekend keeps the same pattern, a Friday evening in the harbor and Santa by boat on Saturday.
facts: Lawson Tower, on First Parish Road, is a water tower dressed as a castle. The Scituate Historical Society says Thomas W. Lawson built it in 1902 to hide a 276,000 gallon, 153 foot steel water tank that his wife Jeannie disliked, using a 15th century watch tower on the Rhine River as the model. Ten bells from the Meneely Bell Foundry in Troy, New York, hang at the top, weighing from 300 to 3,000 pounds, and the tower has 123 stairs.
trains: Scituate has two stops on the MBTA Greenbush Line of the Commuter Rail: North Scituate and Greenbush, the end of the line, at 247 Old Driftway. Trains run from both stations to South Station in Boston, so a December day trip into the city to see the lights works without the car. For a holiday train ride, Edaville in Carver runs a train through its Christmas lights, and the Boston Street Railway Association shares streetcar history for families who love trains.

traditions: Santa makes his grand arrival by boat in Scituate Harbor on the Saturday of Holidays in the Harbor.
A holiday tree built from decorated, hand-painted lobster buoys stands near the Reel Harbor Theater patio.
Horse-drawn carriage rides with Clydesdales loop around the harbor during Holidays in the Harbor.
Local businesses hang decorated wreaths around the harbor, and visitors vote for their favorites.
The Scituate Historical Society's chimer plays Christmas favorites on the tower's ten bells.
South Shore Conservatory and the Atlantic Symphony Orchestra end their holiday concert with a sing-along.
kidfact: Lawson Tower in Scituate looks like a castle, but it was built to hide a giant water tank, and its biggest bell weighs about 3,000 pounds, as much as a small car.
faq: When does Santa arrive by boat in Scituate?

During Holidays in the Harbor, on the Saturday of the first weekend in December. The Scituate Harbor Business Association says Santa makes his grand arrival by boat at 10 am, the morning after the First Friday evening of music, hayrides and tree lightings in the harbor. Check the association's Instagram for the year's full lineup and map.
What is the Lobster Trap Tree in Scituate Harbor?

It is a holiday tree built from decorated, hand-painted lobster buoys, set up near the patio of the Reel Harbor Theater during Holidays in the Harbor. The Scituate Visitors Center calls it a signature New England maritime holiday display, and it makes a good family photo stop on a walk along Front Street.

Lawson Tower was built in 1902 by Thomas W. Lawson to enclose a steel water tank his wife thought spoiled the view. The Scituate Historical Society cares for it today. It is listed as an American Water Landmark and is on the National Register of Historic Places, and its ten bells are still played for concerts.
Can you take the train to Scituate at Christmas?

Yes. The MBTA Greenbush Line stops at North Scituate and at Greenbush, the last stop on the line. Families can ride the Commuter Rail between Scituate and South Station in Boston, which makes a holiday trip into the city to see the lights easy without driving or parking downtown.
